text: Refactoring is the process of improving code structure without changing what the software actually does. Think of it as cleaning and organizing a messy room: the room still has the same furniture and purpose, but it becomes much easier to move around and find things. In programming, this means making the code more readable for humans, not just for machines. A programmer might rename confusing variables, break large functions into smaller ones, or remove duplicated parts. This practice directly addresses "technical debt," which is the extra work created by taking shortcuts in the past. By regularly refactoring, teams save time in the long run and make future changes much safer and simpler.
